sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, on 20.09.2022, 19 year old prosecutrix lodged an FIR in writing alleging that on 01.03.2022, she along with her cousin after darshan at Shiv Temple was returning to home.
On the way, near Sarwahi Pankaj Yadav riding on a motorcycle came and asked her that he likes her and wanted to marry her and took her first of all to Gadasai.
From there, they proceeded for Dindori by bus and from Dindori they proceeded for Jabalpur and from Jabalpur by travelling in a train he took her to Mumbai and kept her in a room.
In the meantime, he committed rape with her.

After completion of work at Belapur he took her at Airport and remained there with her for a period of almost seven months and in this period he continuously violated her and thereafter refused to marry with her and threatened to eliminate her.
FIR was registered.

After investigation,
charge sheet has been filed.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant has no t committed any offence.
He is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
Appellant and prosecutrix both are major.
Prosecutrix on her own had gone with him and had solemnized marriage with him in a temple.
She herself remained with him for a period of more than 7 months and in this period she made no complaint against the appellant.
FIR has been lodged after a delay of almost more than 6 months.

Therefore, it has been prayed that appellant be released on bail.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail.

6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and other material on record and the fact that prosecutrix and appellant both are major, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.

7. It is directed that appellant-Pankaj Yadav be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
